🗓
On October 7,
Russia's Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov
participated
in a regular meeting of the CIS Council of Foreign Ministers,
hosted by Turkmenistan as the current Chair of the Commonwealth, in
the Avaza National Tourist Zone of Turkmenistan
.
Discussions covered
a broad range of issues concerning cooperation within the CIS framework
, including in the context of the Organisation’s 35th anniversary, which is being marked in 2026.
Plans were outlined for
further strengthening foreign policy coordination
and for
enhancing the CIS international profile
.
🤝
The participants engaged in a thorough exchange of views on global and regional developments
. Sergey Lavrov set out Russia’s approach to a number of pressing issues, including the situation in and around Ukraine and the continuing tensions in the Middle East.
👉
Remarks and answers to media questions by Russia’s Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov following the CIS Council of Foreign Ministers
***
The Ministers
adopted a statement
in support of practical steps to prevent an arms race in outer space.
The 2027 Plan for Multi-Level Consultations between the CIS Foreign Ministries
was endorsed.
Following the meeting,
a package of decisions was adopted
, aimed at deepening integration ties in the cultural and academic spheres, as well as in law enforcement and security.
Most of the documents reviewed will be
submitted for adoption to the CIS Heads of State Council on October 9
. Among them are draft statements
on the 35th anniversary of the Commonwealth
and
on the preservation of historical memory
.
🇰🇬
The next meeting of the CIS Council of Foreign Ministers will be held
in Bishkek in April 2027.

🎙
Remarks and answers to media questions
by Russia’s Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov following the CIS Council of Foreign Ministers
(Turkmenbashi, October 7, 2026)
💬
Today, we began with
bilateral talks with my colleague
, Deputy Chairman of the Cabinet of Ministers and Foreign Minister of Turkmenistan
Rashid Meredov
. We focused primarily on
deepening our strategic partnership
, which we consider particularly important, in line with
our Leaders’ directives
.
🇷🇺
🇹🇲
Next year, we will mark the 35th anniversary of
diplomatic relations
, so today we agreed to draw up a programme of events, including exhibitions, the publication of archival documents and cultural events. We will report to
Vladimir Putin
and
Serdar Berdimuhamedov
on matters within our remit that require decisions by our Presidents.
We discussed preparations for
the
#CIS
Council of Heads of State meeting
, which will open tomorrow evening with a formal reception, followed by the main proceedings on Friday.
An environmental Summit of the five Caspian states
will take place later that day, after the CIS Summit.
🤝
Rashid Meredov and I praised our cooperation across all areas
. We attach particular importance to expanding economic, investment and trade ties.
The Intergovernmental Russian-Turkmen Commission on Economic Cooperation
is due to hold its next meeting before the end of 2026.
We share the view that historical memory must be preserved
, especially at a time when Europe is clearly taking a lax approach to the revival of Nazism in a number of countries, with the acquiescence of their ruling circles. We approved plans to erect
a Friendship monument in Ashgabat
in gratitude to the city’s residents who welcomed
people evacuated from besieged Leningrad
during the Great Patriotic War.
We discussed the international agenda, including cooperation within the CIS and in the Caspian region
. We proposed developing ties between Turkmenistan and the Eurasian Economic Union. We also invited Turkmenistan to take an active part in work on
the Eurasian Charter of Diversity and Multipolarity in the 21st Century
.
📄
Full transcript
***
Key points from the answers to media questions
:
•
There are positions that never overlap 100 percent in any body or between any two countries in any region of the world.
Each country has its own national interests, and diplomatic culture means
finding a balance
between them. That is precisely what we did at today’s Council of Foreign Ministers.
• President of Russia
Vladimir Putin
has repeatedly
stated publicly
that the Americans proposed organising talks between Russia, the US and Ukraine, and Moscow agreed on the understanding that
we first needed to hold our elections
, after which we would agree on the timing, venue, agenda and other details.
•
The Kiev regime began doing everything it could to disrupt
the State Duma elections
. Throughout all three days of voting, it carried out
an unprecedented number of terrorist attacks on civilian targets
, including polling stations. Several people were injured, and there was even a fatality.
❗️
As for moving from statements to concrete action, that question should be put to others.
• We held bilateral
talks with the Ukrainians in Istanbul
, but in 2025 Ukraine broke off the process
without explanation
. These were followed by
trilateral talks
between the US, Russia and Ukraine in Abu Dhabi, which were also
broken off, and again not at our initiative
.
• We also
fully accepted
the proposals put forward by the US in August 2025 during
the Alaska Summit
between Russian President
Vladimir Putin
and US President
Donald Trump
.
☝️
So, our conscience is clear.
It is not our fault that
the Americans were unable to withstand unprecedented and brazen pressure from Europe
, which later proudly declared that it had “buried Anchorage”.

item.content:encoded:

🗓
October 7 marks
the 24th anniversary of the signing of
the Charter of the Collective Security Treaty Organisation
(
#CSTO
), the instrument that established the CSTO as an international regional association.
Its
stated purposes
– the strengthening of peace and stability and the collective defence of the independence, territorial integrity and sovereignty of the member states –
remain the cornerstone of mutually beneficial cooperation in a true spirit of alliance
.
On this basis,
the Russian Federation assumed the CSTO
chairmanship
in 2026
under the motto
‘Collective Security in a
#MultipolarWorld
: A Common Goal, a Shared Responsibility’.
In a short span by historical standards, the Organisation, which today brings together six states –
Russia, Armenia, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan
– has made substantial headway and established itself as
a key mechanism for safeguarding regional security
.
The CSTO systematically
addresses the prevention and settlement of crises
and
counters the many challenges and threats to stability
. It continually enhances the combat readiness of the organisation’s Collective Forces and
sustains intensive foreign-policy coordination
.
Drawing upon its considerable experience and advanced security instruments,
the CSTO continues to evolve
, adapting flexibly to changing circumstances.
🛡
In order to strengthen the Organisation’s security capabilities,
the unique combat experience of
the Armed Forces of the Russian Federation
is being drawn upon
– including in
exercises involving the CSTO Collective Forces
held in the Chelyabinsk Region in September and October 2026.
Cooperation in the emerging fields of biological and information security
is likewise gathering pace. Operations conducted by the law-enforcement agencies and security services of the member states to combat
terrorism, illicit drug trafficking, illegal migration and cybercrime
continue to deliver substantial results.
🤝
The development of ties with other international organisations is a key strand of the CSTO member states’ systematic efforts
. Since 2004, the Organisation has held
observer status
at the UN General Assembly.
Priority is being given to deepening cooperation with the CIS and the SCO
, and the roadmap for cooperation among the three organisations in areas of mutual interest continues to be implemented.
A joint conference of the CSTO, CIS and SCO
on security issues in Central Asia and Afghanistan will be held in Moscow on October 15-16.
The memory of
the Soviet Union’s Victory in the Great Patriotic War
remains a cornerstone of our allied cooperation and of our shared enduring values
. The CSTO member states are joining forces to preserve the truth about the heroism of the Soviet people and to prevent any rewriting of history or any distortion or revision of the war’s outcome.
Prospects for expanding multifaceted allied cooperation will be discussed at the forthcoming
session of the CSTO Collective Security Council,
and at
the joint meeting of the Organisation’s Council of Foreign Ministers, Council of Defence Ministers and Committee of Secretaries of Security Councils
. Both will be held in Moscow on November 10-11. Decisions aimed at strengthening the CSTO collective security system are to be signed.
❗️
The further expansion of comprehensive cooperation with the CSTO member States is
a priority of the Russian Federation’s foreign policy
.
